Hence, the correct answer is **"32".**

questions.question: An insect can move in both directions, front and reverse. He moves towards front for 3 minutes and then reverse for 2 minutes. He moves at a speed of 5 metres per minute. In at least how much time he would be able to cover 105 metres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An insect moves towards front for 3 minutes and then reverse for 2 minutes.

 He moves at a speed of 5 metres per minute.

**Calculation:**

The insect moves at a speed of 5 metres per minute. 

It means that the insect can move 5 metres in 1 minute.

He moves towards front for 3 minutes and then reverse for 2 minutes.

In 3 minutes, the insect moves (5 × 3) = 15 metres forward.

Then reverse for 2 minutes, the insect moves (5 × 2) = 10 metres backward.

Clearly, in forward and reverse movement, the insect moves a total of (15 – 10) = 5 metres forward in 5 minutes.

So, the insect moves 1 meter in 1 minute.

For last 3 min insect only move forward so in the last 3 min covered distance = 3 x 5 = 15 m

So,remaining distance = 105 - 15 = 90 min

So other 90-meter insect cover moving forward and backward ( 1 m in 1 min) = 90 min

Total time for covering 105 m= 90 + 3 = 93 min

**∴ It will move 105 meters in 93 minutes.**

questions.question: Which of the following metals can deposit copper from copper sulphate solution?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Metal activity series:**

__
 
• The **metals** are **arranged** in an** activity** order that is known as** metal** **activity series**.
 
• The** more active** metals are present at the** top** of the series whereas the less active metals are put at the** end **of the series.
 
• The metal activity series is as follows- 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6cefd0380cc4b2a487652b9e43c0af0178b98e67bb57fdb52532d0768019f6b7.png] ​

**Importance of the series-**

 
• The metal activity series is used to **predict displacement reactions.**
 
• Metals that are **above hydrogen** in the series can **displace hydrogen** from acids.
 
• Metals that are **below hydrogen** in the series** cannot displace hydrogen** from the acids
 
• **Metals** that are** higher** in the** activity series **can** displace metals **that are **lower **to them from their salts.
 
• For example,** zinc **can **displace copper** from a solution of** copper sulfate **because** zinc **is **above copper** in the activity series.

**Explanation:**__

 
• **Mercury**, **gold**, and **platinum** are** below copper** in the series so **cannot** displace it from its salt solution.
 
• Among the given metals **only iron **can **displace copper** from its** copper sulphate** solution.
 
• This is because** iron** is present **above** **copper **in the metal activity **series.**
 
• The reaction is as follows:** Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO4 + Cu.**
 
• The **blue** color of the** CuSO****4** solution **changes **to **dirty **green of **FeSO4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f2a57d4e36eab42f090d84e83d6a87ae7924b688f4e299bba719eafbe222c93.png] 

Thus, only iron can deposit copper from its copper sulfate solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National income is the total value of a country’s final output of all new goods and services produced in one year.
 
• Methods of measuring national income are:

 
• Expenditure Method - Under this method, we estimate the disposal of income on the purchase of final goods and services.
 
• Income Method - The Income Method measures national income from the side of payments made to the primary factors of production in the form of rent, wages, interest, and profit for their productive services in an accounting year. 
 
• Production method - In this method, national income is measured as a flow of goods and services. This method is also called an **output method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income

 
 
• 
 There are three methods to measure national income:

 
 
• **Income Method**
 
• **Production (Value-Added) Method**
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
 
• 
 Measurement of National Income – Income Method

 
 
• Estimated by adding all the factors of production (rent, wages, interest, profit) and the mixed-income of self-employed.
 
• In India, one-third of people are self-employed
 
• This is the ‘**domestic**’ income, related to the production within the borders of the country
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Production Method
 
 
• Estimated by adding the value added by all the firms.
 
• **Value-added** = Value of Output – Value of (non-factor) inputs
 

 
 
• This gives** GDP at Market Price (MP) – because it includes depreciation (therefore ‘gross’) and taxes (thus ‘market price’)**
 
• To reach National Income (that is, NNP at FC)
 

 
 
• Add Net Factor Income from Abroad: **GNP at MP = GDP at MP + NFIA**
 
• Subtract Depreciation:** NNP at MP = GNP at MP – Dep**
 
• Subtract Net Indirect Taxes: **NNP at FC = NNP at MP – NIT**
 
 
 
• Measurement of National Income – Expenditure Method
 
 
• The expenditure method to measure national income can be understood by the equation given below: 
 
 
• **Y = C + I + G + (X-M),**
 
• where** Y = GDP at MP, C = Private Sector’s Expenditure on final consumer goods, G = Govt’s expenditure on final consumer goods, I = Investment or Capital Formation, X = Exports, X- M = Net Exports (difference between exports (X) and imports (M))**
 
 
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• GDP: Gross Domestic Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced solely within the boundaries of a country, at a specific time.

 
 
• GDP includes the income of foreigners staying in the country.
 
• It excludes the income of nationals of the country staying abroad and also excludes the remittances sent from abroad.
 
 
 
• GNP: Gross National Product is the sum of the money of all the final goods and services produced both within and outside of a country by nationals during a specific period of time.
 
 
• GNP includes remittances.
 
• It excludes income generated locally by non-nationals.

questions.question:
Choose a term to complete the analogy.

Xylem Parenchyma : Food Storage :: Xylem Fibres : _______________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supportive function**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a complex permanent tissue in vascular plants primarily responsible for the conduction of **water and minerals** from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• It is composed of four distinct types of elements: **Tracheids**, **Vessels**, **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibres**.
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma** consists of living cells with thin **cellulose walls**; these cells are specialized for **food storage** (in the form of starch or fats) and the radial conduction of water through **ray parenchymatous cells**.
 
• **Xylem Fibres** are highly elongated, **dead cells** characterized by significantly thickened, **lignified walls** and obliterated central lumens.
 
• The primary biological role of these fibres is to provide **mechanical strength** and **structural support** to the plant body, allowing it to remain upright and resist physical stresses.
 
• In the given analogy, if **Xylem Parenchyma** is associated with its primary role of **Food Storage**, then **Xylem Fibres** must be associated with their primary role, which is the **Supportive function**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conducting Elements**:

 
 
• **Tracheids**: These are elongated, tube-like cells with **tapering ends** and are dead at maturity. They are the chief water-conducting elements in **Gymnosperms** and **Pteridophytes**.
 
• **Xylem Vessels**: These are long, **tubular structures** formed by a row of cells placed end to end. They are the characteristic feature of **Angiosperms** and are highly efficient at **transporting water vertically**.
 
 
 
• **Lignin**: This is a complex organic polymer deposited in the cell walls of **Xylem Fibres**, **Tracheids**, and **Vessels**, providing the necessary **rigidity** and preventing the collapse of the water-conducting tubes under tension.
 
• **Phloem**: Unlike xylem, which conducts water upwards, **Phloem** is responsible for the **translocation of organic nutrients** (food) from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

Consider the following statements regarding the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946:

I. It proposed the formation of a Constituent Assembly with members partly elected by provincial legislatures.

II. The proposed Union government was to exercise control over defence, external affairs and communications.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)** was the final British attempt to devise a **constitutional framework for a united India**.
 
• It proposed a **three-tier federal structure** with a **weak Centre and powerful provinces/groups**.
 
• **Statement I: **The Plan proposed a **Constituent Assembly**, with members **indirectly elected by provincial legislatures** through proportional representation. Princely states were to nominate their representatives. Hence, **Statement I is correct. **
 
• **Statement II: **The proposed **Union (Centre)** was to control only **defence, external affairs, and communications**, along with necessary finances for these subjects. All other powers were vested in provinces and groups. Hence, **Statement II is correct. **

**Thus, both statements are correct → Option 3. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Total strength: **389 members **
 
• **292 from provinces**, **93 from princely states**, **4 from Chief Commissioner’s provinces **
 
 
 
• **Election method: **
 
 
• Indirect election by **provincial legislative assemblies **
 
• Based on **communal representation (General, Muslim, Sikh) **
 
• Through **proportional representation by single transferable vote **
 
 
 
• **Three-tier structure: **
 
 
• **Union (Centre):** Limited subjects
 
• **Groups of provinces (A, B, C):** Intermediate level with autonomy
 
• **Provinces:** Retained maximum powers
 
 
 
• **Grouping of provinces: **

6. And that's why near-future SF remains relevant -- and dangerous -- in the 'post-truth' era."

• **Sentence Q follows Sentence 1** as it immediately expands on the "challenge" mentioned by adding an "additional burden" regarding the logic of fiction versus reality.

• **Sentence P is the next sentence** as it defines the "job" of sci-fi creators in response to the environment described in Sentence R.
 
• **Sentence S follows Sentence P** to complete the grammatical and logical thought regarding what these systems do: mimic patterns "and give us the chance to infer" intentions.

questions.question:
**Which of the following sentence(s) is/are grammatically correct?**

A. Not until he finished the report he realized the error.
B. Had she been informed earlier, the outcome might have differed.
C. Seldom we witness such unanimity among rivals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Only B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sentence A:** "Not until he finished the report he realized the error." 
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically incorrect because it misses inversion after "Not until." The correct form is: "Not until he finished the report did he realize the error."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B:** "Had she been informed earlier, the outcome might have differed."
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct. It is an example of an inverted conditional sentence where "had" is used to introduce the condition.
 
 
 
• **Sentence C:** "Seldom we witness such unanimity among rivals."
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically incorrect because it misses inversion after "Seldom." The correct form is: "Seldom do we witness such unanimity among rivals."
 
 

Correct sentence: *Only Sentence B is correct grammatically.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When using phrases like "Not until" or "Seldom," inversion of the subject and auxiliary verb is required.
 
• Example of inversion:
 
 
• **Incorrect:** Not until he arrived we started the meeting.
 
• **Correct:** Not until he arrived did we start the meeting.
 
 
 
• In conditional sentences, inversion can replace the "if" clause for a formal tone, e.g., "Had she known" instead of "If she had known."
